questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the center of a traffic lane. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide. You can stay to the left or right side of it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: Which brake is more powerful on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders together while giving each rider enough space?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider an adequate space cushion.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist change gears before starting a turn?

options.text: To prevent a sudden power change during the turn
To keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn
To prevent the motorcycle from slowing down

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent a sudden power change during the turn
questions.explanation: Change gears before turning. Shifting during a turn can cause sudden power changes that make the rear wheel skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: Are helmets required when riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a DOT-compliant helmet. Helmets are your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road

questions.explanation: At night, increase your following distance. Slow down and be ready to move to a different lane position.

questions.question: What is the key to making a quick turn on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly in the direction you want to turn. The sharper the turn, the more the motorcycle must lean.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle collisions with cars are caused by drivers failing to yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car collisions happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way. Never assume that drivers will yield, even if they are required to by law.

questions.question: When riding with a group of motorcyclists, should you use a staggered formation?

options.text: No, not when entering or leaving a highway.
Yes, especially when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, not when entering or leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is generally good, but switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What does it feel like if your front tire goes flat?
questions.explanation: Heavy steering means your front tire may be flat. Stop right away and check your tires.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn is ________ a car horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle horn is quieter than car horns. Use it when needed, but do not rely only on your horn for safety.

questions.question: You cannot avoid an obstacle on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Stay seated so the seat protects you.
Hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and hit the obstacle at as close to a 90-degree angle as you can.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance for a motorcycle under normal conditions?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between your bike and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Keep more distance in bad weather or poor conditions.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of the lane when wet. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left track is often best, but it depends on traffic.

questions.question: Where should you carry a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: On the gas tank in front of you.
Stacked against the back of the seat.

questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads.

questions.question: A helmet gives the most protection when it is all of these, except:
questions.explanation: The best helmet meets DOT standards, fits snugly all around, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: With a passenger on your motorcycle, you should do all of these, except:

options.text: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, ride slower and allow more stopping time. The passenger should hold onto the handgrips or your waist firmly, not the back of the bike.

questions.question: A person is considered intoxicated at a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____.
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are intoxicated. You cannot legally operate a motor vehicle if you are intoxicated.

questions.question: How should you stop a motorcycle in a non-emergency situation?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes together. Also downshift as you brake.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background, red, and black markings. It tells drivers about traffic laws. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris collect in which part of a lane?
questions.explanation: Oil and debris from vehicles collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you:

options.text: May go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must not go over the speed limit.
Must go faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not go over the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete a pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. Your position should discourage sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is near.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them visible.
Cover the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, pick a lane position that makes you visible. Cover the clutch and brakes to react faster. Slow down as you enter the intersection. Do not change speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: A motorized bicycle or moped can travel no faster than:
questions.explanation: In California, a motorized bicycle or moped is a two- or three-wheeled vehicle that cannot go faster than 30 miles per hour on flat ground.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one starts.

questions.question: In California, drivers under age 21 cannot operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In California, you must be 21 to drink alcohol. If you are under 21, you cannot drive with any alcohol in your system—even 0.01 percent BAC. Riding a motorcycle after drinking any alcohol is unsafe, even if you are under the legal limit.
